cells.account: No, neither to sign up nor to change a booking (through the link in the confirmation email)
cells.price: Free plan with ads; Pro $11 per seat a month, billed yearly
cells.reminders: Confirmation by email; automatic reminders on Pro

doodle.goodFit: You need a quick list for a single afternoon with a handful of slots, and everyone already knows how a Doodle link works. You can add your own questions, and Doodle's help describes exporting the sign-ups to Excel, without saying which plan that needs.
doodle.lessSuited: You plan shifts across several days and areas. The free plan is limited and shows ads to everyone, and reminders and co-organisers need a paid plan.
doodle.name: Doodle (sign-up sheets)
doodle.summary: Besides its well-known polls, Doodle offers sign-up sheets: you publish time slots with a limit for each, and people sign up through a shared link without an account.

cells.price: Free; you run your own server
cells.reminders: Opt-in email when a shift changes; calendar export
cells.selfHost: Yes; a hosted instance is only offered for Chaos events

engelsystem.goodFit: Your event has hundreds or thousands of helpers in teams, someone on your side can look after a PHP and MySQL server, and you want arrival tracking, worklogs, rewards or a schedule imported from pretalx. It has been used at 37C3, 38C3, 39C3 and other large events.
engelsystem.lessSuited: You run a smaller club event and nobody can set up and maintain a server. An installation appears to be set up for one event at a time, the angel vocabulary can puzzle people outside the hacker scene, and we found no automatic reminder before a shift.
engelsystem.name: Engelsystem
engelsystem.summary: Open-source software for helpers and shifts at large events, built for the Chaos Computer Club's events such as Congress and Camp. Helpers are called angels and are grouped into angel types.

cells.account: No, sign-up by link or QR code
cells.languages: Website in German, English, French and Italian; the app's languages are not stated
cells.price: Free for 1 event with 20 shifts and 20 helper assignments; paid plans from CHF 169 a year
cells.reminders: By email, and by WhatsApp on paid plans

helferplanung.goodFit: You want reminders by WhatsApp, QR-code check-in with live attendance, or assigning helpers by availability on a planning board, and your budget covers a yearly plan. Each helper picks email or WhatsApp, and if WhatsApp fails the message goes by email.
helferplanung.lessSuited: Your event needs more than 20 shifts or 20 helper assignments and there is no budget: the free plan stops there, the Small plan covers one event a year, and unlimited events cost CHF 390 a year. Prices are in Swiss francs, and the software is neither open source nor available to run yourself.
helferplanung.name: helferplanung.app
helferplanung.summary: An online volunteer and shift planner from Switzerland for clubs, festivals and sports events. Helpers sign up through a link or QR code, without an account or an app.

cells.account: No, sign-up by link or QR code
cells.languages: German (the website offers no other language)

helferstube.goodFit: You hold one or two festivals a year, your helpers shouldn't need an account, and a fixed price per event is fine. It knows about stands and cake donations, exports to PDF and Excel, and brings back last year's helpers with one click.
helferstube.lessSuited: You run many small events a year, since each published one costs €19. The website and app appear to be German only, the code is closed, and you cannot run it on your own server.
helferstube.name: Helferstube
helferstube.summary: A German online tool for helper lists at club festivals such as Kirmes, Schützenfest and carnival. Organisers set up stands, shifts and cake donations, and helpers sign up through a link or QR code.

cells.account: No, with an open edit link (work or school accounts may restrict this)
cells.price: Free with a Google or Microsoft account

spreadsheet.goodFit: You run a small one-off event with a few shifts, and everyone knows each other. There is nothing to learn, any layout works, and it costs nothing.
spreadsheet.lessSuited: You have more than a handful of helpers. Nothing stops a shift from being overbooked or a name from being deleted, everyone with the link sees everyone's contact details, and nobody gets reminded.
spreadsheet.name: Shared spreadsheet
spreadsheet.summary: A Google Sheets or Excel file that everyone may edit, where helpers type their names into the shift rows. Small clubs, schools and parent groups often start this way.

cells.reminders: Before every shift, by email, browser push or Telegram
cells.selfHost: Yes, with Docker Compose, or use wirksam.app

wirksam.goodFit: You plan several events a year and don't want to pay per event, your helpers come back and keep one account, and you want the option of running the software yourself.
wirksam.lessSuited: Your helpers won't create an account, even a free one. You need check-in on site, messages by WhatsApp, or languages other than German and English. Or the event is so large that you coordinate thousands of helpers in teams: Engelsystem was built for that.
wirksam.name: WirkSam
wirksam.summary: A free web app for planning volunteer shifts. Organisers describe each task once and the shifts are created from it. Helpers book the slots that suit them and get a reminder before each one.

about.lede: WirkSam was built for church events and community service, where the roster is usually a spreadsheet passed around by email until nobody knows which copy is current.
about.legalIntro: The full detail is in the small print:
about.nameExplainer: The name is a German pun: “wirksam” means effective, and “zusammen” means together. Volunteering works best when people work together, hence WirkSam.
about.title: A small open-source project

account.answer: Yes, a free one, so that each booking belongs to a person and the reminders reach them. Signing up takes an email address and a password. Somebody who was invited opens the link, signs in, and is part of the event.
account.question: Do volunteers need an account?

audience.answer: For anyone who has to staff an event with volunteers: clubs and associations, festivals, schools, youth groups, congregations and church festivals such as Pfingsten or Kirchentag. Organisers plan the shifts and keep track of them, helpers sign up and see their own shifts in one list.
audience.question: Who is WirkSam for?

calendar.answer: Yes. A private subscription link puts your booked shifts into Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, or Outlook and keeps them up to date when something changes.
calendar.question: Can I see my shifts in my own calendar?

cost.answer: Nothing. There is no paid plan and no advertising. WirkSam is a private, non-commercial project.
cost.question: What does it cost?

data.answer: WirkSam stores your name, email address, profile picture, and the shifts you booked. There is no tracking and no analytics, and the only cookies are the ones that keep you signed in. It is run from Germany under the GDPR: you can request a copy of your data, have it corrected, or delete your account for good.
data.question: What happens to my data?

demo.answer: "Try a demo event" sets up an example event with tasks, shifts, and a few teammates, seen either as an organiser or as a helper. You need no email address for it, and the demo is deleted after an hour.
demo.question: Can I try it without signing up?

languages.answer: German and English. The whole app is available in both, in a light and a dark theme, and works on a phone as well as on a computer.
languages.question: Which languages does WirkSam support?

reminders.answer: WirkSam sends a reminder before every shift by email, browser push notification, or Telegram. Each person picks the channel for each kind of notification and can turn any of them off. Everything also lands in an inbox inside the app.
reminders.question: How do reminders work?

reuse.answer: Yes. Copy an event onto new dates and its tasks, shifts, and times come along, landing on the same weekdays as before. The sign-ups do not carry over, so the copy starts with empty shifts.
reuse.question: Can I reuse last year's event?

selfHost.answer: Yes. WirkSam is open source under the MIT licence, and the code is on GitHub at github.com/Blaxzter/wirksam. It runs with Docker Compose, and on your own installation you decide who may register.
selfHost.question: Can I run WirkSam myself?

visibility.answer: Only the people you invite. A new event is private: you add people by email or with a share link. If you make it public, anyone signed in can ask to join, and your organisers still decide who gets in.
visibility.question: Who can see my event?

what.answer: WirkSam is a free web app for planning volunteer shifts. Organisers set up an event and describe the tasks, and the shifts are created from that. Volunteers book the slots that suit them and get a reminder before each one. It was built for church events and community service, but works for any event run by volunteers.

dataCollected.intro: When you create an account and use WirkSam, we process the following personal data:

items.bookings: Booking data (which duty shifts you signed up for)

items.name: Name (as you enter it when you register)

dataCollected.title: Data We Collect

privacy.intro: We take the protection of your personal data seriously. This privacy policy explains what data we collect when you use WirkSam, how we use it, and what rights you have.

legalBasis.description: We process your data based on Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR (performance of a contract) for core account and booking functionality, and Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR (legitimate interest) for security and platform operation. Where we send optional notifications, we rely on your consent (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR), which you can withdraw at any time in your notification settings.
legalBasis.title: Legal Basis

items.account: To create and manage your user account
items.notifications: To send you notifications about your bookings and tasks (email, push, or Telegram if configured)
items.scheduling: To enable duty scheduling and shift booking
items.security: To ensure the security and proper operation of the platform

retention.description: Your personal data is stored as long as your account is active. If you request account deletion, we will erase your personal data without undue delay, unless we are legally required to retain it. If the hosted service is shut down (see the terms of use), we delete all personal data after the announced shutdown date.
retention.title: Data Retention

rights.contact: To exercise any of these rights, contact us at the email address listed above. You also have the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority.
rights.intro: Under the GDPR, you have the following rights:

items.access: Right of access: request a copy of your personal data
items.erasure: Right to erasure: request deletion of your data
items.objection: Right to object: object to processing based on legitimate interest
items.portability: Right to data portability: receive your data in a structured format
items.rectification: Right to rectification: correct inaccurate data
items.restriction: Right to restriction: limit how we process your data

rights.title: Your Rights

email.description: We use Proton Mail to send transactional emails such as booking confirmations and notifications. Proton AG is based in Switzerland and subject to Swiss data protection law. Only your email address and the message content are processed.

bookings.description: When you book a duty shift, you commit to being available at the scheduled time and place. If you can no longer attend, please cancel your booking as early as possible so the shift can be filled by someone else. Organisers and administrators may cancel or reassign bookings if necessary.
bookings.title: Bookings & Cancellations

changes.description: We may update these terms, for example when WirkSam gains new features or the law changes. We will email you about changes at least four weeks before they take effect, together with the new text. If you do not agree, you can object by email or delete your account before that date. If you neither object nor delete your account, the updated terms apply from that date; we will point this out again in the email. The current version is always available on this page.
changes.title: Changes to These Terms

discontinuation.description: WirkSam runs on a single server and is maintained in spare time. We may therefore limit the service, for example by pausing new registrations, accepting no new events, or capping how many events an account can run. We may also shut the hosted service down entirely. We will announce a shutdown by email and on this site, usually at least four weeks in advance, so you can save your plans in good time. The source code remains openly available, so you can keep running WirkSam on your own server.
discontinuation.title: Limits and shutdown

law.description: These terms are governed by the laws of the Federal Republic of Germany.
law.title: Governing Law

liability.description: WirkSam is a free, volunteer-run project. We are not liable for any damages arising from the use of the platform, including but not limited to missed shifts, scheduling conflicts, or data loss. Use the platform at your own discretion.
liability.title: Limitation of Liability

scope.description: WirkSam is a free, non-commercial platform for coordinating volunteer shifts at events, in clubs, congregations and other groups. By creating an account and using the platform, you agree to these terms.
scope.title: Scope of Service

termination.description: You can delete your account at any time from your settings page. All your personal data and bookings will be permanently removed. We reserve the right to deactivate or remove accounts that violate these terms.
termination.title: Account Termination

usage.intro: When using WirkSam, you agree to:

items.lawful: Use the platform only for its intended purpose of volunteer duty scheduling.
items.noAbuse: Not attempt to manipulate, overload, or exploit the platform.
items.reliable: Honor your booked duty shifts or cancel in a timely manner if you cannot attend.
items.respectful: Be respectful to other users and organisers.

usage.title: Acceptable Use

clubFestival.ctaTitle: Try it at your next club festival

account.answer: Yes, with a free account: an email address and a password. That way every booking belongs to a person and the reminder reaches them. Whoever opens an invitation link signs in and is part of the event. If your helpers won't create an account under any circumstances, a tool where people sign up through a plain link suits you better, and our comparison page lists some.
account.question: Do helpers have to register?

cancellations.answer: They cancel the shift in the app and the place is open again straight away. You see it as open in the overview and can ask someone directly. So that shifts aren't forgotten in the first place, everyone gets a reminder beforehand.
cancellations.question: What happens if someone cancels at short notice?

headcount.answer: That depends on how busy it gets. For each stand, think about how many people are needed at the same time in the busiest hour, and plan with that number. Shifts of two to three hours are easier to fill than half a day. In WirkSam you set the shift length and headcount per task, and you can give single days different hours.
headcount.question: How many helpers do I need per stand, and how long should a shift be?

helperList.answer: Create an event in WirkSam with the festival days, and a task for each stand with its hours, shift length and headcount. The shifts are created from that. Then invite your helpers by link or email, and they sign up themselves. It is free, and you need no template.
helperList.question: How do I make a helper list for our club festival?

setup.answer: As tasks of their own with their own hours, for example set-up on Friday from 2 pm and teardown on Sunday from 8 pm. Everyone can then see that these need people too, and teardown doesn't fall to the few who are still around at the end.
setup.question: How do I plan set-up and teardown?

share.answer: Yes. WirkSam prints a roster per task or for the whole event. The plan online stays up to date, and everyone you invited sees the same version.
share.question: Can I print the plan and put it up in the clubhouse?

faq.lede: What organisers usually want to know before the festival.
faq.title: Planning helpers for a club festival

hero.lede: In WirkSam you set up each stand at your club festival as a task, generate the shifts from it, and send your helpers a link. They sign up for themselves, you can see at any time where someone is still missing, and everyone gets a reminder before their shift. It works the same way for a summer fête, a sports day or an anniversary, and it costs nothing.
hero.title: Plan your club festival's volunteer shifts online

chat.description: Someone writes “I'll do the bar on Saturday” in the group chat, three messages later nobody remembers who promised what, and a shift ends up with two people or none.
chat.title: Sign-ups get lost in the group chat

gaps.description: The list hangs in the clubhouse or sits in someone's inbox, and the only way to find out which shifts are still open is to ask around.
gaps.title: Nobody sees the gaps

noShows.description: Weeks pass between signing up and the festival. Without a reminder, shifts slip people's minds, and when someone drops out the news reaches the wrong person.
noShows.title: Forgotten shifts and late cancellations

teardown.description: The stands are planned with care, and on Sunday evening only a few people are left to take the tent down.
teardown.title: Set-up and teardown are an afterthought

versions.description: Every change is typed in by hand and sent round again, until nobody knows which copy is current.
versions.title: Three versions of the same spreadsheet

pains.lede: Most of it comes from the plan being in too many places at once.
pains.title: Where helper planning usually goes wrong

gaps.description: Helpers book the shifts that suit them. You see every stand at once, can hide the shifts that are full, and know exactly where to ask around.
gaps.screenshotAlt: The task list with a week of shifts beside each entry, showing booked and open places per slot.
gaps.title: Watch the gaps close

invite.description: Paste a list of email addresses, or share one invitation link in your club newsletter or group chat. Before the shifts are handed out, members can mark when they are free.
invite.screenshotAlt: The availability page, where a helper marks the hours they are free on each day of the event.
invite.title: Invite your members

nextYear.description: Copy the event onto next year's dates. Stands, shifts and times come along and land on the same weekdays. Nobody is signed up yet.
nextYear.screenshotAlt: The copy-event screen listing last year's tasks with their shift counts, each ticked to come across to the new dates.
nextYear.title: Next year, start from this year's plan

reminders.description: Before each shift WirkSam sends a reminder by email, browser push or Telegram. Anyone who has to drop out cancels in the app, and the place is open again for someone else.
reminders.screenshotAlt: Notification settings with a row per notification type and per-channel switches for email, push, and Telegram.
reminders.title: Everyone is reminded before their shift

setup.description: Plan set-up on Friday afternoon and teardown on Sunday evening as tasks of their own, with their own hours and headcount. On a task's page, every shift shows how many of its places are taken.
setup.screenshotAlt: A task page with its shifts grouped by day, each showing how many of its places are booked.
setup.title: Set-up and teardown get their own shifts

stands.description: Create the event with its dates, then a task for each stand: the bar from 4 pm to midnight, two-hour shifts, three people each. WirkSam works out every shift and shows you a preview before anything is created.
stands.screenshotAlt: The shift schedule form beside a preview of every shift it would create.
stands.title: Each stand becomes a task

steps.lede: An example: a festival from Friday to Sunday with a bar, a grill, a cake stand and a cash desk, plus set-up and teardown.
steps.title: How your club festival could run in WirkSam
